> I’d rather direct my attention toward capturing more complex thoughts that the medium of Blygger affords.

While I’m still mobile-native, might as well expound and accrete on what inspirations I’m pulling from when truesighting the promise of Blygger.

Edits as a quiet primitive of the medium strikes a similar vein as when I found out about version history while reading through the SCP Foundation wiki. Seeing how public editors changed fictional containment documents led to a kind of interstitial storytelling that remained under the surface when reading through what’s merely bureaucratic creepypasta. Kinda like how people hid secret messages in early HTML, but in WikiDot. Also surfaces what kind of creative decisions people made in their writing, made the process just a bit more approachable.

Also kottke.org (a recent find, post-covid) as an Always There, The Whole Time experimental testbed for social media features like the permalink, or even forked off into new platforms (tumblelogs -> Tumblr). What new social templates can naturally develop within a protocol like Blygger?
